lessons.title: Fresh Juices: Mango, Passion, Pineapple
lessons.body: Fresh juice sells fast in African cities, especially near bus parks, markets, and schools. Start with ripe mango, passion fruit, or pineapple. For mango juice, use 2 large ripe mangoes (about 1 kg) per litre of water. Peel, slice, and blend with 500 ml clean water. Strain through a fine sieve or clean cloth. Add 500 ml more water and 4 tablespoons sugar (or honey). Stir well. For passion juice, scoop pulp from 10-12 fruits into 1 litre water. Blend for 10 seconds only to avoid bitter seeds. Strain. Add 4-5 tablespoons sugar. For pineapple, peel one large pineapple, cut into chunks, blend with 1 litre water, strain, and add 3 tablespoons sugar. Always use clean, boiled and cooled water. Bottle in 500 ml plastic bottles. Sell cold. On a hot day, you can sell 50 bottles at 50 cents to $1 each, depending on your location. Keep juice in a cooler box with ice packs. Do not leave juice in the sun. Make small batches twice a day to avoid spoilage. Add a squeeze of lime to mango and pineapple to keep colour and flavour. Label bottles with a marker: flavour and date. Sell within 24 hours. Wash all tools with soap and rinse with boiled water. Your hands must be clean. This is a cash business: start with 10 pineapples, 20 mangoes, or 30 passion fruits. You can double your money in one day if you choose a busy spot.

lessons.title: Hibiscus (Zobo/Sobolo) and Ginger Drinks
lessons.body: Zobo (hibiscus) drink is a top seller across West Africa. Buy dried red hibiscus petals from market. For 5 litres, use 2 cups dried hibiscus, 1 cup fresh ginger (peeled and sliced), 1 pineapple skin (optional for flavour), and 1 cup sugar. Rinse hibiscus in cold water. Put hibiscus, ginger, and pineapple skin in a large pot with 5 litres water. Boil for 20 minutes. Turn off heat. Add sugar and stir until dissolved. Let it cool completely. Strain through a clean cloth. For ginger drink (sometimes called 'ginger beer' but non-alcoholic), use 2 cups fresh ginger, 4 litres water, 1 cup sugar, and juice of 2 lemons. Blend ginger with 1 litre water, strain, then add remaining water, sugar, and lemon juice. No boiling needed. Both drinks can be spiced with cloves, black pepper, or vanilla. Bottle in clean plastic bottles. Keep cold. Zobo lasts 3-4 days in a fridge or cooler with ice. Ginger drink lasts 5 days. Sell at 50 cents to $1 per 500 ml. Display in a clear cooler with ice. Add a few mint leaves for look. Wash bottles with hot water and soap before filling. Never use dirty bottles. You can make 20 litres per day in a large pot. Start with 1 kg hibiscus and 1 kg ginger. Profit is high: 1 kg hibiscus costs about $2 and makes 10 litres. Sell 10 litres at $0.75 per 500 ml = $15. That is a good daily income.

lessons.title: Fermented Drinks: Mahewu and Mageu
lessons.body: Mahewu (or mageu) is a traditional fermented maize drink, popular in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Zambia. It is cheap to make and very refreshing. You need maize meal (fine white or yellow), water, and a little sugar. For 5 litres: mix 2 cups maize meal with 1 litre cold water to make a smooth paste. Boil 4 litres water. Add the paste slowly, stirring to avoid lumps. Cook for 15 minutes until thick. Add 1 cup sugar and stir. Let it cool to room temperature (about 25-30Â°C). Add 2 tablespoons of previous mahewu (or 1 teaspoon dry yeast) as a starter. Cover with a clean cloth and leave in a warm place for 24-48 hours. It will become slightly sour and bubbly. Stir well, then strain if you want a smooth drink. Bottle and keep cold. Mahewu is best drunk within 3 days. It has natural probiotics and gives energy. Sell in 500 ml bottles for 30-50 cents. You can also add flavour like lemon or ginger. In rural areas, mahewu is sold at bus stops and markets. Start with 5 kg maize meal. One batch of 20 litres costs about $3 and sells for $10-$15. Always use clean containers. If it smells bad or grows mould, throw it away. Fermentation is safe if you keep everything clean and use a good starter. You can make it daily: cook in the morning, ferment overnight, sell next day. Many customers prefer it slightly sour. Adjust fermentation time to taste.

lessons.title: Coffee and Tea Service
lessons.body: Coffee and tea are quick profits. In East Africa, serve strong black coffee (like Ethiopian or Kenyan). In West Africa, serve tea with milk and sugar (like 'African tea' or 'chai'). You need a thermos, cups, a kettle, and a small stove or fire. For coffee: buy roasted beans, grind them, or use instant coffee. For 1 litre: boil 1 litre water. Add 3-4 tablespoons ground coffee. Stir, let sit 2 minutes, then strain. Or use 2 tablespoons instant coffee. For tea: boil 1 litre water with 2 tea bags or 2 teaspoons loose tea. Add 1/2 cup milk and 3 tablespoons sugar. For ginger tea, add sliced ginger. Serve hot in 200 ml cups. Sell at 30-50 cents per cup. A thermos keeps drinks hot for 4 hours. Set up near a taxi rank, market, or office in the morning. You can sell 100 cups in 2 hours. Costs: 1 kg coffee makes about 100 cups. 1 kg tea leaves makes 200 cups. Milk and sugar add cost. But profit margin is 60-70%. Add a small snack like mandazi or biscuits to increase sales. Keep cups clean: wash with soap and rinse with hot water. Use a clean cloth to wipe. Never reuse cups without washing. For iced coffee or tea, brew strong, cool, add ice, and sell in plastic cups. But hot drinks sell better in cold mornings. Start with one thermos, 50 cups, and a small table. Reinvest profits into a bigger thermos and more cups. This business works anywhere people wait.

lessons.title: Iced Drinks and Smoothies
lessons.body: Iced drinks and smoothies sell best in hot afternoons. You need a blender, ice, fresh fruit, and a cooler. For a simple smoothie: blend 1 cup chopped mango, 1/2 cup pineapple, 1/2 cup water, and 1 cup ice. Add 1 tablespoon sugar or honey. Blend until smooth. Pour into 300 ml cups. Sell for $1-$1.50. For a green smoothie: blend 1 cup spinach, 1 banana, 1/2 cup pineapple, 1 cup water, and ice. For iced tea: brew strong tea, cool, add lemon and ice. For iced coffee: mix 1 cup strong coffee, 1/2 cup milk, 1 tablespoon sugar, and ice. Always use clean ice made from boiled water. Never use ice from unknown sources. Keep fruit cold before blending. Wash all fruit well. Use a clean blender jar and cups. Sell from a small stall with a table, cooler, and a sign. List flavours and prices. On a hot day, you can sell 50 cups in 3 hours. Costs: fruit and ice are cheap if you buy in bulk. A cup of smoothie costs about 30-40 cents to make; sell for $1. Profit is good. Add a straw and a napkin. Keep the stall clean. Change the menu weekly: use seasonal fruits like watermelon, banana, or avocado. For avocado smoothie, blend 1 avocado, 1 cup milk, 1 tablespoon sugar, and ice. It is filling and popular. Always ask customers if they want sugar. Offer a loyalty card: buy 5, get 1 free. This builds repeat business. Start with 10 cups and one blender. You can grow from there.

lessons.title: Pricing and Displaying Beverages
lessons.body: Pricing is simple: know your cost per bottle or cup, then add 100% to 200% profit. For example, if a 500 ml juice costs 30 cents to make, sell for 60-90 cents. If a cup of tea costs 10 cents, sell for 30 cents. Always round to a friendly price: 50 cents, $1, $1.50. Do not undercharge. Customers respect a fair price. Display your drinks in a clean cooler with ice. Use a clear plastic box or a wooden stand. Put a white cloth on the table. Arrange bottles in rows: juices in front, zobo behind, water on the side. Use a handwritten sign with big letters: 'Fresh Juice $1', 'Zobo 50c', 'Cold Water 30c'. Write in the local language and English. Keep the cooler lid closed to keep cold. Use ice packs or frozen water bottles instead of loose ice to avoid mess. For hot drinks, use a thermos with a tap. Put cups upside down on a clean cloth. Have a small bin for rubbish. Wear clean clothes and a apron. Smile and greet every customer. Offer a small taste of juice for free to new customers. Keep a small notebook to record sales: what you sold, how many, and money. At the end of the day, count your money and subtract costs. If a drink is not selling, reduce price or change flavour. If it sells out fast, make more next day. Location matters: near schools, bus parks, markets, and construction sites. Sell where people are hot and thirsty. Start small, keep records, and grow.

quiz.q: What is the correct ratio of ripe mangoes to water for mango juice?
options: A) 2 large mangoes per 1 litre water
quiz.explanation: The lesson states to use 2 large ripe mangoes (about 1 kg) per litre of water.

quiz.q: Why should you blend passion fruit pulp for only 10 seconds?
options: A) To keep the colour bright
quiz.explanation: Blending too long releases bitterness from the seeds.

quiz.q: How long should fresh juice be sold within?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says to sell fresh juice within 24 hours to avoid spoilage.

quiz.q: What ingredient is added to mango and pineapple juice to keep colour and flavour?
quiz.explanation: A squeeze of lime helps maintain colour and flavour.

quiz.q: For 5 litres of zobo, how much dried hibiscus is used?
quiz.explanation: The recipe uses 2 cups dried hibiscus for 5 litres.

quiz.q: How long does zobo last in a fridge or cooler with ice?
quiz.explanation: Zobo lasts 3-4 days when kept cold.

quiz.q: What is a key difference between making zobo and ginger drink?
options: A) Zobo requires boiling, ginger drink does not
B) Ginger drink requires boiling, zobo does not
quiz.explanation: Zobo is boiled, while ginger drink is made without boiling.

quiz.q: What is the typical profit from 1 kg hibiscus costing $2?
quiz.explanation: 1 kg hibiscus makes 10 litres, selling at $0.75 per 500 ml = $15.

quiz.q: What is the main ingredient in mahewu?
quiz.explanation: Mahewu is a fermented maize drink.

quiz.q: How long should mahewu ferment?
quiz.explanation: Fermentation takes 24-48 hours in a warm place.

quiz.q: What can be used as a starter for mahewu?
quiz.explanation: A previous batch or dry yeast acts as a starter.

quiz.q: How long is mahewu best drunk within?
quiz.explanation: Mahewu is best within 3 days.

quiz.q: What should you do if mahewu smells bad or grows mould?
quiz.explanation: Bad smell or mould means it is unsafe and should be discarded.

quiz.q: For 1 litre of coffee, how much ground coffee is recommended?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says 3-4 tablespoons of ground coffee per litre.

quiz.q: How many cups can 1 kg of coffee make?
quiz.explanation: 1 kg coffee makes about 100 cups.

quiz.q: What is a good location for selling coffee and tea?
options: A) Near a taxi rank or market
quiz.explanation: Busy waiting areas like taxi ranks and markets are ideal.

quiz.q: What should you add to increase sales with coffee or tea?
options: A) A small snack like mandazi
quiz.explanation: Adding a snack increases sales.

quiz.q: What is the profit margin for coffee and tea?
quiz.explanation: The lesson states a 60-70% profit margin.

quiz.q: What type of ice should you use for smoothies?
options: B) Ice made from boiled water
quiz.explanation: Always use ice made from boiled water to ensure safety.

quiz.q: How much does a cup of smoothie cost to make?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says a cup costs about 30-40 cents to make.

quiz.q: What is a good way to build repeat business for smoothies?
quiz.explanation: A loyalty card (buy 5 get 1 free) encourages repeat customers.

quiz.q: What fruit is suggested for a filling smoothie?
quiz.explanation: Avocado smoothie is filling and popular.

quiz.q: What is the recommended profit margin when pricing beverages?
quiz.explanation: The lesson says to add 100% to 200% profit.

quiz.q: How should you display cold drinks?
options: A) In a clear cooler with ice
B) In a bucket of hot water
quiz.explanation: A clean cooler with ice keeps drinks cold and attractive.

quiz.q: What should you use instead of loose ice in a cooler?
options: A) Ice packs or frozen water bottles
quiz.explanation: Ice packs or frozen bottles avoid mess and keep things cold.

quiz.q: What should you write on your price sign?
options: C) Both local language and English
quiz.explanation: Using both languages helps all customers understand.

quiz.q: Why should you keep a small notebook?
options: A) To record sales and costs
quiz.explanation: Recording sales and costs helps you track profit and make decisions.

quiz.q: What should you do if a drink is not selling?
options: A) Reduce price or change flavour
quiz.explanation: Adjusting price or flavour can boost sales.

quiz.q: What is a good location for selling cold drinks?
options: A) Near schools and construction sites
quiz.explanation: Hot, thirsty people gather at schools, markets, and construction sites.

quiz.q: What should you do before filling bottles for zobo or juice?
options: A) Wash with hot water and soap
B) Rinse with cold water only
quiz.explanation: Clean bottles prevent spoilage and illness.
